sprueche: Giving the flowers a sip of water…
Brushing the fur to maximum fluff…

tips: Hoofbeats reveal the ground: sand sounds soft, wood hollow, stone bright — and mud slows your horse down.
Petting your horse during a break grants a second wind once per ride when stamina runs out.
Galloping drains stamina. Drop into a walk now and then so your horse can recover.
Time your jumps: take off just before the obstacle to earn a "Perfect" rating.
Brushing, feeding, mucking out — a well-groomed horse bonds with you faster.
After a rain shower, check the evening sky: with a little luck a rainbow appears.
Foxes and fireflies roam at night, while meadow and sky belong to the birds by day.
The ford at the creek is shallow enough to ride through — take the bridge to stay dry.
Wild horses graze far out in the meadow valley. Approach slowly or they will flee.
Every zone wants to be discovered: the lookout on the ridge shows you the whole region.
The old barn in the southwest keeps a secret. A ride out there is worth it.
Ducks waddle across the jetty at the lake — the pond is especially pretty in the evening.
Tölting horses carry you swiftly without tiring. Not every breed can tölt.
If your horse spooks, keep a calm pace: the fright passes after a few seconds.
Hay rustles when you fill the trough — hungry horses thank you with a whinny.
The tournament grounds lie southeast of the yard: rails, wall and oxer want clean jumps.
Villagers with tasks wait in Hufingen. The dirt road at the village edge leads you there.
The weather can be planned: the daily forecast tells you when rain rolls in — great for dry rides.
Thunderstorms sound mighty but are harmless. Sheltering in the stable still feels cozy.
A foal inherits values from both parents — pick the breeding pair with care.
Training is specific: lots of galloping builds speed, lots of jumping builds jump power.
The dirt road connects every zone. Follow it and you will never get lost.
Bonding pays off: a trusting horse spooks less and answers the reins more finely.
A deep snort means your horse is exhausted — give it a break at a walk.
The stable can be upgraded: more boxes mean room for new horses.
Saddle up, mount, go — "Ride out!" takes you from the yard into the open region.
Music and sound effects can be adjusted separately in the settings — to your taste.
Rain makes the ground wet and muddy. Allow a little extra time after a shower.
